scope: D3D8 implicit depth binding helpers retain no public surface reference because the root device owns cached storage. D3D8 primary color binding already uses root-owned storage. D3D9 standalone and implicit primary/auto-depth surfaces use binding_refs, with device-cache ownership preventing physical destruction on last implicit unbind. Additional chain buffers and ordinary texture/cube views retain their current binding model. Reset treats every implicit public reference as external; private binding slot counts are not deducted. Two old sources strictly compile and fail at real binding helper public-count assertions. Native cached helper/getter loops run 128 rounds/256 zero revivals per API, plus existing actual full setter/Reset/private lifetime suites. XP uses complete SDK setters/getters, 32 rounds/64 revivals per API, borrowed rebinds, two public-zero Clear/Present frames, two refused Resets and one accepted Reset per API, existing cached identity/private-data retention across Reset and six protected finalizers per API across post-Reset final device, binding-only final device and last public surface orders. Native implicit private-store Reset semantics remain open; this phase preserves the existing project cache behavior. D3D8 blocked Reset returns DEVICELOST and D3D9 INVALIDCALL, preserving the already validated API-specific contract. No original HAL/game/FPS claim, general device state preservation with external children, arbitrary callback/thread/device-loss graph, additional-chain/other resource public binding counters, full formats/MSAA/fullscreen/multiple buffers/rotation, or review stages 4/5/6 completion. Host/protocol/shader/bundle unchanged.
